tasks.short: Assess learning needs through surveys, interviews and consultation, then agree training priorities.

steps.what: Agree the assessment scope with managers.
Prepare survey questions and interview prompts.

loop.input: Assessment scope and approved question bank.
loop.output: Assessment questions linked to the scope.
loop.check: Check scope coverage and prohibited questions; specialist checks neutrality, accessibility and relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per assessment; unresolved issues return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse approved questions first; a bounded loop adapts wording to unfamiliar learning needs.

steps.what: Send the survey and collect responses through a form.
Interview employees and facilitate focus groups about work barriers.
Combine survey results with role and training records.
Summarise recurring needs and distinguish training gaps from other barriers.

loop.input: Minimised survey text, consultation notes and aggregate needs dataset.
loop.output: Needs brief with source references, themes and unresolved explanations.
loop.check: Validate references and counts; specialist checks minority views and training versus process explanations.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass per batch; ambiguous themes remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Counts are deterministic, but varied descriptions of work barriers require interpreting free text.

steps.what: Agree priorities, owners and non-training referrals with managers.

tasks.design: Configure assessment forms and reminders in the {WORKFLOW}, then join permitted {HCM} and {LMS} records on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Bounded loops prepare questions and a referenced needs brief in the {DOCS}; the specialist conducts consultations and managers approve priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms already handled collection, but records used different identifiers and interpreting work barriers required context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, configurable forms and faster integration development make the plumbing cheaper. Bounded text processing can prepare material for review without settling priorities.
tasks.still_hard: Employees may withhold sensitive concerns. Training gaps can resemble poor tools, workload problems or unclear management expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, probe contradictions and recognise when a training request masks a different problem.

ambition.what: A work-barrier diagnostic that routes process problems to HR and managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time compiling responses and more time testing explanations with employees. They gain a proposed referral mandate; managers still decide resources and priorities.

reach.task: Investigate recurring employee concerns behind training requests.
reach.learn: Confidential intake, referral thresholds and how to distinguish individual concerns from organisational patterns.

evidence.claim: Configurable forms, record joins and bounded text summaries can support training-needs assessment; this is a design estimate.
Trust-building and separating learning needs from work-design problems usually require human consultation.

assumptions: This describes a typical mixed workflow, not a confirmed customer process.
The time split follows the consultation-heavy prior; a mailbox is not assumed to be the main intake channel.
Survey sending uses an approved internal audience and question set.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and include access, privacy review and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; identifiable responses are minimised and access restricted.
unknowns: Which forms, identifiers and export permissions are available?
Are surveys anonymous, confidential or attributable, and what reporting group sizes are permitted?
Which national consultation rules and existing employee agreements apply?
Can the specialist refer non-training problems directly to HR or managers?
research_questions: How reliably can reviewed themes distinguish skill gaps from process barriers?
Does the question bank cover the languages and accessibility needs of participants?
new_work: Review drafted questions and source-linked themes.
Handle missing identifiers and suppress unsafe reporting groups.
Maintain the question bank, referral categories, access controls and retention settings.

tasks.short: Record training participation, monitor progress and evaluate whether programmes improve work.

steps.what: Record attendance, completions and certificates in the learning system.
Export learning records and combine them with role and outcome data.
Check records and calculate participation, completion and outcome measures.
Read learner and manager feedback and summarise recurring concerns.

loop.input: Minimised learner and manager feedback, grouped by programme.
loop.output: Feedback summary with referenced themes and contrary examples.
loop.check: Validate references and theme counts; specialist checks omissions, privacy and unsupported conclusions.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction pass per programme batch; uncertain comments remain uncategorised.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed ratings need no model; open comments use varied language and contain contextual explanations.

steps.what: Interpret results with managers, considering work changes and other explanations.
Approve programme actions and record the evaluation conclusion.

tasks.design: Configure completion recording in the {LMS} and connect approved {HCM} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The {BI} calculates agreed measures, while a bounded loop summarises feedback into the {DOCS}; people interpret effectiveness and approve programme actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion reporting was available, but linking learning to work outcomes required manual joins and agreement on meaningful measures.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting features and small integrations can remove compilation work. A bounded loop reduces feedback reading time without claiming causal proof.
tasks.still_hard: Changes in staffing, workload or tools can explain outcome differences. Small groups, missing data and delayed effects limit conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose credible measures, challenge causal claims and decide whether a programme deserves investment.

ambition.what: Monthly review of programmes with weak completion or transfer-to-work signals.

tasks.altitude: The specialist replaces recurring export work with investigation of weak signals and conversations with managers. They gain a proposed right to initiate programme reviews, while funding decisions stay with the training manager.

reach.task: Decide which programmes to continue, change or stop.
reach.learn: Evaluation design, uncertainty, opportunity cost and how to present evidence for investment decisions.

evidence.claim: Completion recording, scheduled joins and configured dashboards are established deterministic capabilities; no training-specific case is supplied.
Completion and satisfaction alone do not establish that training caused better work outcomes.
AI intended to monitor or evaluate worker performance can fall within Annex III employment uses; programme-level reporting requires an intended-use assessment.

assumptions: A typical company records completions in the {LMS}, with a spreadsheet bridging outcome sources.
The structured-data prior supports more deterministic automation than the task's overall judgement-heavy label suggests.
Completion recording uses approved criteria and verified attendance, not model-generated competence scores.
Build ranges include access checks, metric validation, a pilot and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; the proposed dashboard evaluates programmes rather than ranking workers.
unknowns: Which outcome measures exist and can lawfully be linked to learning records?
Does the {LMS} receive verified attendance and assessment results automatically?
Are the reports currently used in promotion, discipline or other employment decisions?
Which national consultation rules, retention limits and reporting thresholds apply?
research_questions: Which measures detect transfer to work without introducing excessive employee monitoring?
Can comparison groups or repeated measurements support stronger conclusions for priority programmes?
new_work: Resolve failed joins, disputed completions and missing outcome data.
Review feedback summaries and investigate unusual dashboard results.
Maintain metric definitions, cohort rules, access permissions and intended-use limits.

tasks.short: Design orientation and training programmes, prepare materials and organise delivery.

steps.what: Agree learner outcomes, audience and delivery constraints with stakeholders.
Design the learning sequence, practice activities and assessment approach.
Draft learning materials, exercises and facilitator guidance.

loop.input: Programme plan, approved source material and selected templates.
loop.output: Draft learning materials with source references and labelled gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections and source references; specialist reviews learning alignment, accessibility and examples.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per module; missing facts become questions for the expert.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but adapting explanations and practice scenarios requires bounded language generation.

steps.what: Validate technical accuracy and approve the learning materials.
Coordinate instructors, rooms and dates through messages and calendar checks.
Publish approved courses and enrol the agreed employee audience.
Brief instructors and decide whether the programme is ready to start.

tasks.design: Use approved templates in the {DOCS} and a bounded drafting loop to produce materials from a human-designed programme plan. A scheduling workflow checks the {CALENDAR}, and configured {LMS} rules publish approved content and enrol agreed audiences after content and schedule approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reusable templates existed, but adapting materials took time and scheduling crossed documents, messages and learning records.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster development makes small scheduling and publishing connections economical. Source-constrained drafting can prepare materials for specialist and expert review.
tasks.still_hard: Good learning design depends on realistic practice and learner context. Technical accuracy, accessibility and customer-specific obligations still need accountable review.
tasks.human_edge: Design practice that changes behaviour and judge whether learners can use it in their actual work.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time designing practice and briefing instructors, with less document assembly and scheduling. They gain a proposed right to adapt activities within approved outcomes and budget.

reach.task: Coordinate new-starter orientation and track readiness.
reach.learn: Joiner triggers, role eligibility, enrolment exceptions and the handoff from orientation to workplace practice.

evidence.claim: Template generators, constraint-based scheduling and configured enrolment can reduce programme administration.
Bounded drafting can adapt approved material, but instructional quality and technical correctness need review.

assumptions: The steps describe employee programmes; customer delivery requires an explicit external audience and publishing policy.
Creation and consultation dominate the time split, consistent with the priors; scheduling messages are a smaller component.
The expert can approve content, and the specialist can approve schedules within an existing budget.
Build ranges cover a reusable pilot workflow, not the creation of an entire course library.
Access and consultation ranges include national employee consultation where audience assignment or employee-data use changes.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; source material and learner data use approved access and retention settings.
unknowns: Which course templates, content formats and publishing interfaces are supported?
Who approves content, enrolment criteria and customer-facing publication?
Are instructors and rooms represented consistently in the {CALENDAR}?
Which languages, accessibility requirements and national consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Which modules can use existing approved materials without substantial rewriting?
Can the publishing workflow preserve accessible formats and course version history?
new_work: Review generated explanations, exercises and source references.
Handle scheduling conflicts and enrolment exceptions.
Maintain approved sources, templates, publishing rules and accessibility checks.

tasks.short: Diagnose weak training results, develop alternatives and test a revised approach.

steps.what: Review evaluation evidence for programmes missing expected improvements.
Discuss barriers with learners, instructors and managers.
Develop alternative methods, exercises and pilot designs.

loop.input: Barrier hypotheses, approved materials, method library and capacity limits.
loop.output: Alternative methods and a draft pilot plan with explicit hypotheses and measures.
loop.check: Validate constraints and references; specialist checks pedagogical fit, accessibility and testability.
loop.stop: At most three alternatives and one revision per programme; weak options return to manual design.
loop.why_not_simpler: A method library supplies reusable patterns, but adapting practice to a contextual barrier needs language drafting.

steps.what: Select a method and approve pilot scope, safeguards and measures.
Arrange the approved pilot and coordinate instructors and participants.
Compare pilot outcomes against the agreed baseline and success criteria.
Interpret pilot results and decide whether to revise, expand or stop.

tasks.design: Configure the {BI} to flag missed programme targets and calculate pilot comparisons from approved measures. A bounded loop in the {DOCS} adapts a method library into alternatives, while the {WORKFLOW}, {CALENDAR} and {LMS} coordinate approved pilots; people diagnose barriers and decide adoption.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hard part was contextual diagnosis, not computation. Alternatives were developed from scratch, and small pilots required repeated coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable method library, deterministic pilot tracking and faster workflow development reduce preparation costs. Bounded drafting helps explore alternatives but does not establish that they will work.
tasks.still_hard: Weak results may come from work conditions rather than teaching methods. Small samples and delayed behaviour change make pilot interpretation expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Form useful hypotheses, design realistic practice and recognise when further training would waste learners' time.

ambition.what: A rapid learning-method pilot service for struggling programmes.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week diagnosing barriers and designing experiments. They gain a proposed mandate to prepare small pilots within an agreed envelope; the training manager approves launch and wider adoption.

reach.task: Address organisational barriers that training cannot resolve.
reach.learn: Change diagnosis, manager accountability and how work design affects skill application.

evidence.claim: Reusable method libraries, pilot workflows and deterministic comparisons can support training redesign.
Drafting alternatives does not demonstrate effectiveness; contextual diagnosis and observed pilot outcomes remain necessary.

assumptions: This models a redesign cycle through pilot evaluation; instructor delivery is separate work.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained in diagnosis and adoption, while preparation and pilot administration remain open to change.
Scheduling and enrolment stay within the approved pilot plan; deviations become exceptions.
Build ranges assume reuse of the evaluation data pipeline and exclude the elapsed time needed to observe learning outcomes.
Access and consultation ranges include employee consultation under applicable national rules where pilot participation or data use changes.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; pilot comparisons do not automatically trigger individual employment decisions.
unknowns: Is there an approved method library and a reliable baseline?
Who can authorise pilot time, budget and participation?
How long must outcomes be observed before a useful comparison is possible?
Which national consultation rules and learner-data permissions apply?
research_questions: Which pilot designs can distinguish a teaching-method problem from lack of workplace opportunity?
Can alternatives be tested without disadvantaging participants or withholding required training?
new_work: Review drafted methods and remove unsupported assumptions.
Maintain the method library, pilot templates and success criteria.
Handle scheduling exceptions, monitor pilot execution and document uncertain results.

role.altitude: The specialist's week shifts from compiling records and assembling materials toward consultation, learning design and programme experiments. Proposed decision rights cover diagnostic referrals and adaptations within approved plans; managers retain resource and adoption decisions.
reach: Human resources specialist: investigate employee concerns behind learning requests.
Human resources assistant: connect orientation readiness with enrolment and workplace practice.
Training and development manager: support programme investment decisions with credible evaluation.
Human resources manager: resolve work-design barriers that training cannot fix.
skills_to_grow: Learning design and realistic practice development.
Evaluation design, causal reasoning and uncertainty.
Data definitions, privacy-aware reporting and integration exception handling.
Review of generated material against approved sources.
role.ambitious_version: Run a learning-improvement service that diagnoses work barriers, builds role-specific practice pathways and tests alternatives through small approved pilots.
